finding.why: onboarding_screen_test.dart's testWidgets + childAwareText tests are near-line-for-line duplicates of onboarding_bulk_l1_test.dart's 'profileCreation phase' and 'childAwareText helper' groups (same button text, same disabled-state check, same ACTIVE-badge tap, same substitution cases) — it reads like the pre-L1 file the L1 rewrite was meant to replace but never deleted. learning_process_wizard_service_test.dart runs the same scenario (e.g. noReview creates one לימוד stage) through two differently-named group blocks repeatedly, several pairs marked '(F2 variant)' — roughly half of its 31 tests are redundant with the other half. Every future behavior change to these services must be updated in 2 places or the suites silently diverge.
finding.recommendation: Delete onboarding_screen_test.dart (fully superseded) or trim it to whatever the L1 suite doesn't cover. In learning_process_wizard_service_test.dart, merge each '(F2 variant)'/second-group pair into the first, keeping the more specific assertions from each.
acceptance_criteria: Total test count in the 2 files drops by the number of confirmed-duplicate cases with no coverage regression on the 2 lib files under test

finding.title: BulkPriorCompletionService.execute()'s profileId branch bypasses DI and its bookmark write is never asserted
finding.why: When execute() runs with a non-null profileId — the live path add_track_flow_screen.dart uses when a parent adds a track for a specific child — the service `new`s up a BookmarkRepositoryImpl directly instead of using the injected _bookmarkRepository, so no test double can intercept it (no seam). bulk_prior_completion_service_test.dart's execute() tests never pass profileId, so that branch never runs there at all. bulk_prior_completion_siyum_detection_test.dart does pass profileId (lines 333, 372) so the branch does run against a real in-memory DB, but neither test reads back the bookmarks table afterward — the branch's correctness (right profileId, right track resolved) is completely unverified. A bug here would silently point a child's bookmark at the wrong profile/track with no test failure.
finding.recommendation: Parameterize bookmarkRepositoryProvider as a .family(profileId) (or inject a BookmarkRepository factory into BulkPriorCompletionService) so the profileId path goes through the same injectable seam as the rest of the class; add an assertion in bulk_prior_completion_siyum_detection_test.dart that reads back the bookmark row for the target profile and checks it points at the expected sefariaRef.
acceptance_criteria: A test calls execute(profileId: X) and then asserts (via a real or fake repository read) that the bookmark was written under profile X
bulk_prior_completion_service.dart contains no direct `BookmarkRepositoryImpl(` construction outside a provider

finding.title: Extract onboarding intro-page Color(0x...) literals into core/theme constants
finding.why: The same navy (0xFF1A36A5) is hand-typed as a private constant independently in all 3 files (19 raw Color literals total: 6+2+11), instead of one shared source. A future rebrand or dark-mode pass for the intro carousel requires finding and updating every hex literal by hand, with no compile-time link tying the copies together if one drifts out of sync. This is exactly the pattern the (currently non-functional) no_color_literal_outside_theme custom lint targets.
finding.recommendation: Add the ~8 distinct hex values used across the 3 files to AppColors/AppTheme (or an onboarding-scoped palette class in core/theme/) and import it instead of redefining per file.
acceptance_criteria: Once custom_lint is fixed, dart run custom_lint reports zero no_color_literal_outside_theme violations under lib/features/onboarding/presentation/widgets/

finding.title: Localize the hardcoded '…yos' decorative chip text in IntroMishnaIllustration
finding.why: The sibling chip on the same illustration correctly resolves via AppLocalizations (introMishnaReviewChip: 'Review…' EN / 'חזרה…' HE), but this second floating chip is a literal, unlocalized Latin-script fragment rendered unconditionally regardless of locale. In Hebrew locale a user sees a stray Latin '…yos' fragment floating over an otherwise fully-Hebrew first-run screen. No test in app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's dedicated l10n-leak regression group — whose stated purpose is guarding this exact screen against exactly this class of bug — catches it, because that group checks a different text element on the same page.
finding.recommendation: Add an ARB key for the fragment with a real Hebrew value (or drop it for HE if the design intent doesn't survive translation), and extend app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's Hebrew l10n group to assert on it.
acceptance_criteria: make arb-parity and flutter analyze stay clean after adding the key
app_intro_screen_l1_test.dart's 'l10n — Hebrew locale renders Hebrew, not English literals' group gains an assertion that the English fragment does not appear in Locale('he')
